text: Young Lamin was the swiftest oarsman on the Barra shore.
His carved pirogue cut through the surf like a flying fish, and his holds always returned brimming with barracuda and silver bonga.
'The elders speak of spirits because their arms have grown weak,' Lamin boasted to the young crewmen gathered on the beach.
'The fish at Sita Nunku belong to whoever has the courage to drop a net into the dark water.'
Despite Elder Baboucar’s solemn warning that the equinox moon stirred forces no net could hold, Lamin pushed his boat out into the gathering swell.
